title: Kaktarua (কাকতাড়ুয়া) - 3-minute pitch v2: cinematic 3D field + sci-fi system walkthrough
structure: 0:00-0:30 problem (field) | 0:30-1:00 solution (phone, real app UI) | 1:00-2:00 system flow (sci-fi) | 2:00-2:30 AI approach (sci-fi) | 2:30-3:00 impact + next step (field + map)
notes: Every claim matches the code or a measured run: pipeline per backend/app/services/scans.py; threshold 0.60 (domain/decision.py); retrieval = metadata filter + keyword overlap on contextual chunks, NO vector search yet (domain/kb_search.py); validator V1-V6 (domain/advice_validator.py); BRRI yield figures from the KB factsheets; app screens are real captures of the live app (20 Nov 2026). lines.text: Afternoon in a Bangladeshi paddy field. Rice feeds the nation, grown on small family farms.
But Rahim's leaves are turning brown, and there is no expert nearby to ask.
The Bangladesh Rice Research Institute warns that blast can cut yield by up to eighty percent, and bacterial leaf blight by about thirty.
One wrong guess means the wrong spray and wasted money.
So he opens Kaktarua, a Bangla-first app that works on any phone.
He photographs one sick leaf. Location data is stripped, and photo quality is checked first.
AI names the disease, here brown spot with medium confidence, or honestly says I am not sure below a sixty percent threshold.
Advice comes only from BRRI factsheets, in plain Bangla, every step with its source.
Inside the system: the photo leaves the React app on Vercel and reaches our FastAPI backend on Render.
First, the upload is hardened: type and size checks, a decompression-bomb guard, and GPS data removed by re-encoding.
Second, a local quality gate. A blurry or dark photo abstains before any AI call.
Third, Meta's Muse Spark vision model answers in strict JSON, choosing from nine rice diseases with a confidence score.
Below zero point six, the decision engine returns not sure. Above it, retrieval pulls up to eight BRRI passages for that disease.
The advice model writes Bangla steps from those passages only, and validator rules V1 to V6 check every citation, number and word.
Three matching scans in one division within a week create a draft outbreak alert. Nothing reaches farmers until a human approves it.
The model cuts the leaf into patches, turns each into a vector, and attention weighs every patch against the others.
Softmax of Q K transpose over root d, times V. Linear algebra, repeated billions of times, scores each disease.
Retrieval is contextual: thirty-nine BRRI passages, each with an AI-written context line. Vector search comes next.
Our MCP server exposes the same knowledge, and over one thousand automated tests guard the pipeline.
Back in the field, Rahim knows what to do, and calls the agriculture office before any chemical.
Our vision: every rice farmer in all eight divisions, with an honest second opinion in their pocket.
Our targets: zero wrong advice shown, verified outbreak alerts within a week, and fewer unnecessary sprays.
Kaktarua. Honest help for every rice field.
